gml:Dictionary.gml:description: Codes classifying the analysis method used in a low-strain integrity test - ASTM D5882's two named methods (Pulse Echo Method, time-domain; Transient Response Method, frequency-domain), which the French national standards NF P94-160-2 (reflection/sonic-echo method) and NF P94-160-4 (impedance method) register as two separate documents rather than one standard with an internal method choice. Used for the value of diggs:LowStrainIntegrityTestType/testMethod.
gml:Dictionary.gml:name: DIGGS Low Strain Integrity Test Method Codelist Definitions

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pile head motion (velocity, from an accelerometer or geophone) is measured as a function of time following hammer impact, and the time-domain record is evaluated directly for reflections indicating a change in impedance - a discontinuity, void, or the pile toe. ASTM D5882's Pulse Echo Method; corresponds to the French reflection/sonic-echo method, NF P94-160-2.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Pulse Echo Method (PEM)

diggs:Definition.gml:description: Pile head motion and force (the latter from an instrumented hammer) are measured as a function of time and the data are evaluated in the frequency domain via the mobility (velocity/force) spectrum. ASTM D5882's Transient Response Method; corresponds to the French impedance method, NF P94-160-4.
diggs:Definition.gml:name: Transient Response Method (TRM)
